questions.q: New Zealand voted on 7 November. Whose centre-right coalition leads on preliminary results?
questions.f: His National–ACT–NZ First bloc has 67 of 131 seats so far, with final results due 27 November.

questions.q: Israel's President Herzog gave the first chance to form a new government to which former army chief?
questions.f: 67 members of the Knesset recommended him, against 46 for Benjamin Netanyahu.

questions.q: Russia and Ukraine held their first direct talks in about nine months in which city?
questions.f: The US-mediated talks ended with agreement on a large prisoner exchange.

questions.q: Stephen Miller became White House chief of staff this week, replacing whom?
questions.f: Wiles, the first woman in the job, moves to Donald Trump's political operation.

questions.q: Pope Leo XIV made the first papal visit in nearly four decades to which country?
questions.f: President Javier Milei greeted him in Buenos Aires before he moved on to Peru.

questions.q: Spain's first general strike in 14 years was driven mainly by anger over what?
questions.f: The 24-hour strike by the UGT and CCOO unions disrupted transport, ports and factories.

questions.q: A magnitude 5.7 earthquake in central Japan on Sunday was centred in which prefecture?
questions.f: About 22 people were hurt, mostly in neighbouring Aichi, and there was no tsunami warning.

questions.q: Which south-east Queensland city was worst hit by power cuts after Wednesday's supercell storms?
questions.f: More than 81,000 homes in the south-east lost power, almost 60,000 of them in Logan.

questions.q: Which department store chain, now in receivership, named 19 stores it will close?
questions.f: Closures include Robina and Sunshine Plaza in Queensland and the chain's only NZ store.

questions.q: Qantas will cut about 850 corporate jobs under a technology deal with which firm?
questions.f: Most of the roles are Sydney-based and many will move overseas.

questions.q: John Setka has been expelled for five years from which union?
questions.f: The union's administrator expelled him after 27 charges; Setka denies wrongdoing and plans to appeal.

questions.q: Todd Russell, who died this week aged 54, survived a 2006 mine collapse in which Tasmanian town?
questions.f: He and Brant Webb were trapped underground for 14 days; tributes came from across the country.

questions.q: Which Cape York town recorded its hottest November day on record, 39.8°C, last Saturday?
questions.f: The far-north heatwave came the same weekend storms cut power to Sarina.

questions.q: Which big four bank reported a full-year cash profit of about $7.6 billion, up 31%?
questions.f: It declared a final dividend of 83 cents a share.

questions.q: The November Westpac–Melbourne Institute survey put consumer sentiment at its lowest in how many years?
questions.f: Sentiment among mortgage holders hit the lowest level since the series began in 1994.

questions.q: US October inflation came with no annual figure. Why?
questions.a: The 2025 government shutdown stopped data collection
w: A cyber attack on the statistics bureau
A change in the index base year
questions.f: Prices still rose 0.4% in the month, above the 0.3% forecast.

questions.q: US Federal Reserve governor Christopher Waller said what should be considered in December?
questions.f: He linked it to core inflation of 0.3% or more, which the October data then delivered.

questions.q: Oil prices slid on Monday after Donald Trump signalled restraint towards which country?
questions.f: Brent crude had already fallen 16% the week before.

questions.q: Who is Nvidia's interim CEO after Jensen Huang resigned?
questions.f: Kress stays on as chief financial officer, and Harvey Jones becomes the board's first chair.

questions.q: The US FDA added a new warning to all GLP-1 drugs such as Ozempic about a rare risk to what?
questions.f: The condition, NAION, is a rare stroke of the optic nerve that can cause vision loss.

questions.q: The WMO says 2026 will be among the four warmest years. Which year still holds the record?
questions.f: 2024 averaged about 1.55°C above pre-industrial levels; January–September 2026 was 1.47°C.

questions.q: Bayer's asundexian, newly approved in the US, is meant to prevent what?
questions.f: It is the first approved drug of its class, blocking a clotting protein called factor XIa.

questions.q: David Jones will close 19 stores. How many stores did it have?
questions.f: That is half the network, with closures by the end of December.

questions.q: The Westpac–Melbourne Institute consumer sentiment index fell to what level in November?
questions.f: Any reading below 100 means pessimists outnumber optimists.

questions.q: By roughly how much did the number of new investor home loans fall in the September quarter?
questions.f: The 30.6% fall was the biggest on record, almost double the previous record drop.

questions.q: China's trade surplus for January–October passed what mark for a second year running?
questions.f: October exports alone rose 35.2% on a year earlier.

questions.q: About how many lightning strikes did Energex record during Wednesday's south-east Queensland storms?
questions.f: More than 400 powerlines came down and Brisbane Airport recorded a 96 km/h gust.

questions.q: COP31, where Chris Bowen is 'President of Negotiations', opened in which Turkish city?
questions.f: The summit runs from 9 to 20 November under an Australia–Türkiye arrangement.

questions.q: The federal government announced a new safety regulator with penalty powers for which industry?
questions.f: Companies will have to allow independent testing of their models and report incidents.

questions.q: Victorians vote on 28 November. Who is the Labor Premier going into the election?
questions.f: Carroll replaced Jacinta Allan as Premier in July; Jess Wilson leads the Liberals.

questions.q: Queensland is investigating possible fraud in a financial assistance scheme for whom?
questions.f: Payouts rose from about $100 million to nearly $244 million in 2024–25.

questions.q: The COP31 host country now officially styles its name how?
questions.f: The UN adopted the spelling in 2022 at the country's request.

questions.q: Remembrance Day marks the 1918 Armistice. The word 'armistice' comes from Latin roots meaning what?
questions.f: It joins 'arma' (arms) with '-stitium', a stopping or standing.

questions.q: David Jones is in receivership. A receiver is usually appointed by whom?
questions.f: Receivers FTI Consulting are acting for the lender Hilco.

questions.q: This week's storms were 'supercells'. What sets a supercell apart from an ordinary thunderstorm?
questions.f: The rotating updraft, called a mesocyclone, lets supercells last for hours.

questions.q: Gadi Eisenkot was handed the 'mandate' to form a government. The word comes from a Latin verb meaning what?
questions.f: Latin 'mandare' is often explained as 'to give into the hand'.

questions.q: David Jones is closing 19 of its 38 stores. What percentage is that?
questions.f: 19 ÷ 38 = 0.5, exactly half.

questions.q: The Armistice was signed in 1918. How many years ago was that, as of this Remembrance Day?
Tasmanian MPs are getting a 22% pay rise. How many dollars is 22% of $140,000?
In the asundexian trial, repeat strokes fell from 8.4% on placebo to 6.2%. How many percentage points is that?
questions.f: 8.4 − 6.2 = 2.2, which is roughly a 26% relative reduction.

questions.q: The Kangaroos play which team in Sunday's Rugby League World Cup final at Suncorp Stadium?
questions.f: Australia beat Samoa 44–12 in their semi-final, with a Reece Walsh hat-trick.

questions.q: Who won Formula 1's rain-hit São Paulo Grand Prix?
questions.f: Verstappen was second; Piastri climbed from 10th on the grid to finish sixth.

questions.q: Which England replacement scored two tries in two minutes in the 45–22 win over the Wallabies?
questions.f: It was England's highest score ever against Australia.

questions.q: Which batter was left out of Australia's Test squad for the home series against New Zealand?
questions.f: Chair of selectors George Bailey said a recall is still possible.

questions.q: Dolly Parton's final recorded vocal features in a duet on the new album by which band?
questions.f: The track 'Torn' closes the album 'Carnaval de Luz', released on Friday.

questions.q: Which song extended its record run at No. 1 on the US Billboard Hot 100 to 27 weeks?
questions.f: Ella Langley's hit holds the record for the most weeks at No. 1.

questions.q: Which rock star paid tribute to Beaconsfield survivor Todd Russell at a Sydney concert?
questions.f: Grohl wrote 'Ballad of the Beaconsfield Miners' after the 2006 rescue.

questions.q: Which film topped the US box office with the biggest opening ever for a live-action foreign-language film?
questions.f: It took US$30.5 million, beating the record set by 'Hero' in 2002.

questions.q: Which film was No. 1 at the Australian box office last weekend?
questions.f: It was the first time foreign-language films held the top two spots here.

questions.q: Physical copies of which video game reached shops this week, still locked until its 19 November launch?
questions.f: Digital buyers could start preloading the game on 10 November.
